newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 26.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- BUSINESS GIVEN WELFARE ROLE

At a meeting of prominent businessmen at 10 Downing Street on Wednesday, chancellor Gordon Brown notified those in attendance that the business community will be an essential factor in the success of the government's flagship 'welfare to work' programme for the long-term unemployed. The three billion sterling programme to be launched next April is to be funded by the windfall tax on privatised utilities and was met by no opposition at the meeting.
-- B.A.T HEAD SAYS PACT WILL NOT CUT TEENAGE SMOKING

Martin Broughton, chief executive of British tobacco and insurance group B.A.T Industries, has described targets set by the settlement between the U.S. tobacco industry and the U.S. government to drastically reduce teenage smoking as 'unrealistic'. Broughton fully expects to 'fail to meet' the targets, comments that should prove damaging to the White House and Congress as it reinforces the belief common among anti-smoking groups that the settlement benefits the tobacco companies more than society.
-- STRIKE THREATENS FLIGHTS CHAOS FOR BA

An overwhelming 73 per cent of The Transport and General Workers Union's staff, which represents 9,000 of British Airways' 12,000 cabin staff, have voted in favour of strike action. BA's chief executive Robert Ayling said he does not believe the staff wanted to strike, but that they were being 'held back by 1970's trade unionism'. Should the strike proceed, summer flights at BA will face severe disruption, as many flights from Heathrow and Gatwick airports will have to be cancelled.
-- TRADE DEFICIT UP 43 PER CENT AS IMPORT VOLUMES SOAR

Fears concerning the sustainability of the UK consumer boom and interest rates were raised once again on Wednesday, as it was announced that the UK's global trade deficit rose 43 per cent in April to about one billion sterling, on import volumes at their highest level for 16 years. While the Office for National Statistics stated the figures could be a statistical anomaly, economists expressed concern due to the incompatibility of the trade figures and recent 'out of control' consumer spending.
-- FRANCE TELECOM SELL-OFF EXPECTED IN AUTUMN

The French government has revealed that it may begin the partial privatisation of France Telecom as early as September or October of this year, ahead of next year's liberalisation of Europe's telecoms markets. The privatisation, possibly the largest in France's history, will raise funds to recapitalise struggling state-owned companies while reassuring markets of the pragmatism of the country's government, but is expected to strain relations between it and the opposition Communist party.
-- BECKETT SET TO GET TOUGH ON BASS DEAL

Trade and Industry secretary Margaret Beckett has announced a series of extreme conditions on the merger between Bass Brewers and Carlsberg-Tetley -- a merger which would create Britain's largest brewing group -- but is not expected to block the deal. The government has agreed to the conditions, having said further concentration in the industry was unnecessary. Through the merger, Bass wo uld control about 35 per cent of the UK beer market, the largest such stake. Bass and Carlsberg say the merger is essential to restore profitability following the introduction of government industry reforms.
-- ONLINE HEALTHCARE SUPPLIER LAUNCHED

Procurement Health has launched an Internet-based procurement service, Procurenet, which carries a database of 10,000 companies and is endorsed by the NHS Confederation. The site will offer an Internet-based procurement service for NHS Trusts, family doctors and private hospitals and nursing homes. Procurenet will supply a comprehensive range of healthcare items, including drugs, dressings, and operating theatre equipment.
-- ANDERSEN STRIFE OVER CHOICE OF HEAD

Partners of Andersen Worldwide, the world's largest accounting and consulting organisation, have rejected the board's nomination of a new chief executive for a second time, sending Anderson into turmoil once again. The Candidate, George Shaheen, failed to receive the necessary two-thirds majority vote from the 2,700 partners as did Jim Wadia earlier this month, indicating reluctance to vote for a chief executive from outside their own firm.
-- EUROTUNNEL RECEIVES BOOST OVER PLAN TO RESTRUCTURE

Christian Cambier, head of the Association of Eurotunnel Shareholders, has declared that he will support the company's restructuring plans if its operating concessions licence is extended. Eurotunnel officials claim that an extension to the concession is essential to persuade its 730,000 investors to back the 8.5 billion sterling restructuring plan.
